title: SGS Weekly Recap: Top 5
tagline: The week in power: where the world leaned, and why.
discovery_note: Overall, the week leaned Slightly Globalist.

stories.headline: Poland vetoes the EU content law
stories.summary: Poland's president vetoed the EU online-content law. It would have let officials order fast takedowns. He said a judge, not an office, should decide.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: Poland blocked an EU speech-control law and kept the call with courts.
stories.what_it_means: A court still decides what speech comes down.
stories.economic_impact: Poland may face pressure from Brussels over the veto.
stories.everyday_example: It's like refusing a takedown without a judge.

stories.headline: FAA nationwide ground stop
stories.summary: The FAA halted every US departure for more than four hours, the longest stop since 9/11. Officials blamed a contractor's network upgrade, with no confirmed cyber attack.
stories.label: Slightly Globalist
stories.why: A contractor-owned central network went down, and the whole country stopped flying.
stories.what_it_means: One contractor's network can stop the whole country's flights.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a crew tripping power for every airport.

stories.headline: UK would follow EU food rules
stories.summary: Britain and the EU finished a draft food deal. It cuts border checks, but Britain follows EU food rules with no vote, and the EU court has the final say.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: A nation agrees to take its food laws from Brussels with no vote.
stories.what_it_means: Brussels would write Britain's food laws.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a faster lane with a rewritten list.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi talks, only a prisoner swap
stories.summary: In Abu Dhabi, a US idea would let Russia claim Donbas and send Russian gas to Europe through a US middleman. Talks ended with a prisoner swap, but no land deal.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: Ukraine's borders were negotiated by outsiders; nothing settled.
stories.what_it_means: Outside powers are sketching a nation's borders.
stories.economic_impact: War costs and Europe's gas squeeze go on.
stories.everyday_example: It's like neighbors redrawing your fence.

stories.headline: Iran tightens its grip on Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran said it destroyed navigation aids in the Strait of Hormuz. The UN says twenty-five seafarers were killed. Officials in Iran said tankers hit mines, not verified, and also threatened undersea cables.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: A state is gating a shared sea lane; strong state power is not sovereignty.
stories.what_it_means: One country is using a shared sea lane as a weapon.
stories.economic_impact: Shipping costs push up fuel prices.
stories.everyday_example: It's like mining the shared driveway.
